extracted.intended_audience: astronomers / natural philosophers and observational astronomers
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and evaluative principles for observing comets, interpreting their tails, and correcting/deriving cometary trajectories (orbital plane, nodes, inclination, areas, periods) from three or more accurate observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congruence of observations with theory to establish identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Congruunt igitur hae observationes cum theoria quatenus congruunt inter se, & congruendo probant unum & eundem fuisse cometam, qui toto tempore a quarto die Novembris ad usque nonum Martii apparuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require independent observations to agree both with one another and with the theoretical trajectory; mutual agreement of observations and theory is evidence that they concern the one same comet. Use multiple observers' measurements (positions relative to fixed stars preferred) to confirm identity across dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer positional measurements (positions to fixed stars) over azimuths/altitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: Crassiores sunt observationes Pofithcei & Cellii, ese praesertim quae per azimuthos & altitudines capiebantur... meliores sunt eae quae per positiones cometae ad fixas a Montenaro, Hookio, Angone & observatore in Nova Anglia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating observational quality, favor measurements given as positions relative to fixed stars (plate-sky positions); azimuth and altitude measurements are coarser and less reliable for precise trajectory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory must reproduce observed irregular (inequable) motion to be accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Motus ejus fuit maxime inaequabilis... Et theoria, quae motui tam inaequabili per maximam coeH partem probe respondet, quaeque easdem observat leges cum theoria planetarum, & cum accuratis observationibus astronomicis accurate congruit, non potest non esse vera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid theoretical model is one that reproduces the observed pattern of acceleration and deceleration, corresponds with planetary laws, and aligns with accurate astronomical observations; match detailed time-varying motion, not only average motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tail measurements: angular length, width, inclination and variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Nov. 18 cauda ... visa fuit longa ... Dec. 12 cauda transibat per medium Sagittae... Denique Feb. 10 caudam oculis armatis aspexi gradus duos longam. ... caudae luce tenui micabat ad longitudinem graduum 6 vel 7; ... luce tenuissima ... longitudinem graduum duodecim & paulo ultra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record tail length and width in angular measurements (degrees, minutes) relative to nearby stars/constellations; note sensitivity to sky conditions (serene sky reveals more of faint tail), and record inclination of tail chord relative to circle through Sun and comet; report when tail appears/disappears and how its length/brightness evolve with time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses on tail origin and criteria to reject optical explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Caudarum triplex opinio; eas vel jubar esse solis per translucida capita propagatum, vel oriri ex refractione lucis in progressu ipsius a capite cometae in terram, vel denique nubem esse seu vaporem a capite cometae jugiter surgentem & abeuntem in partes a sole aversas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider three rival hypotheses (sunbeam transmitted through translucent nucleus; refraction of light in celestial medium; cloud/vapour emitted from nucleus). Reject 'jubar' and refraction hypotheses on grounds: (a) light is only visible where reflected by matter; (b) tails do not change colors as refraction would predict; (c) telescopic amplification increases star brightness enormously without producing tails, contradicting an optical/refraction origin. Conclude tails derive from reflecting matter emitted by the nucleus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of reflecting material in tail to produce visible light
rubrics_metrics.description: Lux non cernitur quatenus in jubare est, sed quatenus inde reflectitur ad oculos nostros. Requirltur Igltur materia aliqua reflectens in regione caudae, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To account for observed tail illumination, posit particulate matter in the tail that reflects sunlight toward observers; absence of reflecting matter cannot produce the observed localized tail brightness against the dark sky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of telescopic tests to distinguish material tail from optical artifact
rubrics_metrics.description: Sciendum est quod lux fixarum plus centum vicibus augeri potest mediantibus telescopiis, nec tamen caudae cernuntur. Planetarum quoque lux copiosior est, caudae vero nullae: cometae autem saepe caudatissimi sunt...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tails were merely optical transmission/refraction effects, telescopes that greatly amplify light should produce similar tails for stars/planets; they do not—thus use telescopic comparison as a diagnostic test against optical/refraction explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric method to estimate age of tail vapour (time from nucleus to tail terminus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quo temporis spatio vapor a capite ad terminum caudae ascendit, cognosci fere potest ducendo rectam a termino caudae ad solem, & notando locum ubi recta illa trajectoriam secat... Unde verior erit problematis solutio, ut recta illa, quae orbem secat, parallela sit longitudini caudae, vel potius (ob motum curvīneum cometae) ut eadem a linea caudae diverg at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To infer when vapour at the tail terminus left the nucleus, draw the line from tail end toward the Sun and note where this line intersects the comet's orbital plane; correct for the comet's prior motion (vapour ascends obliquely), so use the more accurate construction (parallels/divergence) described to compute the interval (example: a vapour at Jan 25 began ascending before Dec 11 → implies tail age determination by this geometric procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of tail curvature and deviation to nucleus motion and ascent obliquity
rubrics_metrics.description: Quod deviatio caeteris paribus minor est ubi cauda obliquior est ad orbem cometae, ut & ubi caput cometae ad solem propius accedit; ... Quod curvatura major est ubi major est deviatio, & magis sensibilius ubi cauda caeteris paribus longior est: nam in brevioribus curvatura aegre animadvertitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret curvature/deviation of tail as consequence of combination of vapour ascent direction and comet motion: deviation angle is smaller near the nucleus and larger toward tail end; convex side tends to be brighter and better defined. Use these geometric/qualitative signatures to infer ascent obliquity and relation of tail to nucleus motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamics and persistence of tails: vapour rarefaction and conservation of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Vapor non recta ascendit a sole, sed motum cometae, quem ante ascensum suum habebat, retinendo & cum motu ascensus suus eundem componendo ascendit oblique.... Cauda autem, quamdiu apparuit, ex vapore fere omni constabat, qui a tempore perihelii ascenderat; & vapor, qui primus ascendit & terminum caudae composuit, non prius evanuit quam ob nimiam suam tam a sole illustrante quam ab oculis nostris distantiam videri desiit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that vapours ascend rapidly near the Sun, then slow under gravity; early-emitted particles form long-lasting tail components which persist until they are too faint to detect. Tails produced near perihelion can be long and bright and may remain visible for significant time; dynamics (retention of previous motion) cause tails to follow elliptical motions similar to nuclei.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric rarity computations justify thin vapour composing tail
rubrics_metrics.description: Vapores autem, qui spatiis tam immensis implendis sufficiant, ex cometarum atmosphaeris oriri posse, intelligetur ex raritate aeris nostri... inde per computationem ... inveni quod aer, si ascendatur a superficie terrae ad altitudinem semidiametri unius terrestris, rarior sit ... Ideoque globus aeris nostri digitum unum latus ... impleret omnes planetarum regiones usque ad sphaeram saturni & longe ultra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scaling arguments of atmospheric density (comparison with Earth's atmosphere and gravitational/compression laws) to show that even very rarified cometary atmospheres can supply sufficient vapour to produce observed tails and yet remain translucent to starlight; include estimates showing tail rarities explain translucence of background stars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about attributing irregular tail features to intrinsic comet behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: De caudarum agitationibus subitaneis & incertis, deque earum figuris irregularibus, quas nonnulli quandoque describunt, hic nihil adjicio; propterea quod vel a mutationibus aeris nostri & motibus nubium caudas aliqua ex parte obscuraiitium oriantur; vel forte a partibus viae lacteae, quse cum caudis praetereuntibus confundi possint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating apparent sudden disturbances or irregular tail shapes, account for terrestrial atmospheric variations, clouds, and confusion with Milky Way structures rather than immediately ascribing structural changes to comet itself; note observational contamination sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of head brightness vs tail growth as evidence of material loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Notandum est quod cometa mense Decembri, ubi ad solem modo incaluerat, caudam emittebat longe majorem & splendidiorem quam antea mense Novembri... Et qui utrumque viderant, majorem describunt cometem priorem. ... Ex incremento caudae & decremento splendoris manifestum est, quod caput a sole recessit, eique proximum fuit sub initio ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing comet evolution, use the inverse relation between head brightness and tail size (post-perihelion tail growth and head dimming) as indicative of consumption/expansion of nucleus material; compare eyewitness accounts across dates to infer consumption of head material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting celestial refraction as cause due to inconsistent directional deflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Porro si cauda oriretur ex refractione materiae caelestis, & pro figura coelorum defiecteretur de solis oppositione, deberet deflexio illa in iisdem coeli regionibus in eandem semper partem fieri. Atqui cometa anni 1680 Decemb. 28 ... et cometa anni 1577 Dec. 29 ... utroque in casu terra versabatur in eodem loco, & cometa apparebat in eadem coeli parte: in priori tamen casu cauda cometae declinabat angulo graduum 4 aquilonem versus; in posteriore vero ... declinatio erat graduum 21 in austrum. Igitur repudiata coelorum refractione superest ut phaenomena caudarum ex materia aliqua lucem reflectente deriventur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical examples of identical sky geometry producing different tail deflections to argue against an hypothesis of tail deflection by refractive celestial media; directional inconsistencies with refraction imply material origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stepwise operational algorithm to correct an assumed comet trajectory (Propositio XLII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operatio i: Assumatur positio plani trajectoriae ... seligantur tria loca cometae observationibus accuratissimis definita & ab invicem quam maxime distantia ... Ex his locis apparentibus inveniantur, per operationes trigonometricas, loca tria vera cometae in assumpto illo plano trajectoriae. Deinde per loca illa inventa ... describatur sectio conica: & ejus areae ... sint D & E; nempe D area inter observationem primam & secundam, & E area inter secundam ac tertiam. Sitque T tempus totum, quo area tota D + E velocitate cometae ... describi debet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the multi-step correction: (1) assume an orbital plane, pick three well-separated observed positions, compute true positions in that plane by trigonometry, construct conic section through those points, compute areas between observations and corresponding times. This is the baseline operation for trajectory correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic variations to refine node longitude and inclination (Operations 2 & 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oper. 2: Augeatur longitudo nodorum plani trajectoriae, additis ad longitudinem illam 20' vel 30' quae dicantur P; & servetur plani illius inclinatio ... Oper. 3: Servetur longitudo nodorum in operatione prima, & augeatur inclinatio plani trajectoriae ad planum eclipticae, additis ad inclinationem illam 20' vel 30' quae dicantur Q. ... deinde ex observatis praedictis tribus cometae locis apparentibus inveniantur in hoc novo plano loca tria vera ... & tempus totum t quo area tota ... describi debeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To explore sensitivity and find corrections, systematically vary node longitude by small increments P (20'–30') while holding inclination fixed, and separately vary inclination by small increments Q while holding node fixed; recompute true locations and areas to obtain alternate area-time measures (d,e and S,e) needed for solving correction equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve linear relations for correction multipliers and compute corrected orbital elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Jam sit C ad i ut A ad B, & G ad i ut D ad E, ... signis + & - probe observatis quaerantur numeri m & n ea lege, ut sit 2 G - 2 C - mQ^2 - m g - nQ^2 - n y, & 2 T - 2 S aequale m T - m t + n T - n r. Et si in operatione prima I designet inclinationem plani trajectoriae ad planum eclipticae & K longitudinem nodi alterutrius, erit I + nQ vera inclinatio plani trajectoriae ad planum eclipticae & K + mP vera longitudo nodi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate and solve for scalar multipliers m and n from the given proportion/equations relating area ratios and times; apply m and n to compute corrected inclination (I + nQ) and corrected node longitude (K + mP). Then compute corrected semilatus rectum and transverse sides using provided algebraic formulae; from transverse side derive orbital period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining periodic times and transverse semiaxes requires inter-apparition comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Coeterum cometarum revolventium tempora periodica & orbium latera transversa haud satis accurate determinabuntur, nisi per collationem cometarum inter se, qui diversis temporibus apparent. Si plures cometae, post aequalia temporum intervalla, eundem orbem descripsisse reperiantur, concludendum erit hos omnes esse unum & eundem cometam, in eodem orbe revolventem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ascertain orbital periods and transverse semiaxes accurately, compare comet orbits across separate apparitions; identification of the same orbit at equal time intervals confirms periodicity and allows determination of orbital dimensions.
